 Boca Juniors snatches the title from Rosario in the 96th minute
 Boca captain Leandro Paredes hoists the trophy aloft.
 www.imago-images.de
 A last-second goal, wild celebrations in Buenos Aires, and a rival already celebrating: Boca Juniors clinched the Argentine league title in a wild season finale.
 Linus Hämmerli 
 Today at 09:10 • Today at 09:12 Here's what it's all about
 Boca Juniors defeated Defensa y Justicia 1-0 thanks to Enner Valencia (96').
 With 63 points, Boca clinches the Tabla Anual ahead of Rosario Central (62) and is crowned Argentine champion.
 After its 2-0 victory, Rosario Central initially celebrates what it believes to be the title—until news arrives from Buenos Aires.
 Summary created with Unbridled jubilation at La Bombonera, ecstasy in the La Boca neighborhood. Part of Buenos Aires is in an uproar. It’s the 96th minute when substitute Enner Valencia slots the ball into Defensa y Justicia’s net. 1–0! Boca Juniors have achieved their goal. What had been a nerve-wracking evening of soccer just moments ago has turned into a blue-and-yellow celebration.
 For a long time, it looked as though the title would go to Rosario. There, Rosario Central had done what was required with a 2-0 victory over Estudiantes de Río Cuarto. Since Boca could not manage more than a 0-0 draw at the same time, the players and fans already considered themselves champions. Fans stormed the field, and players embraced one another.
 But about 300 kilometers to the southeast, newcomer Valencia was in the process of rewriting the script. After a botched defensive play by goalie Matías Borgogno, the Ecuadorian was in just the right spot and scored the goal that clinched the title for Boca.
 While the stands at La Bombonera were shaking, a sense of disillusionment set in in Rosario. The news of Boca’s late goal didn’t reach the revelers until some time later. In the end, just one point separates the two teams. Boca celebrates winning the Tabla Anual and, with it, the championship title.
